inputs.instruction: Read project/src/entities/taskDefinition.js, project/src/entities/taskInstance.js, project/src/entities/user.js. Report their exact export signatures and the ftm:clientSequence + ftm:updatedAt field shapes. Also read SPEC §5 and §5.1 (lines 292-340 of project/family-task-manager-spec.md) for StateAdapter and conflict-resolution requirements.

Create ONE new file. JavaScript ESM. No new dependencies. before: null.

File - project/src/adapters/state/inMemoryStateAdapter.js:

The canonical in-memory StateAdapter per SPEC §5 and §5.1. Pure JS (no TypeScript); interface is documented via JSDoc.

At the top of the file, JSDoc typedefs for the StateAdapter interface:
  @typedef {Object} InstanceFilter
    Optional fields: assignedTo, status ('pending'|'completed'), taskDefinitionId, fromDate (ISO-8601), toDate (ISO-8601)
  @typedef {Object} StateAdapter
    Methods: saveTaskDefinition(td) -> Promise<void>; getTaskDefinition(id) -> Promise<object|null>; listTaskDefinitions(filter?) -> Promise<object[]>; saveTaskInstance(ti) -> Promise<void>; getTaskInstance(id) -> Promise<object|null>; listTaskInstances(filter?) -> Promise<object[]>; saveUser(u) -> Promise<void>; getUser(id) -> Promise<object|null>; listUsers() -> Promise<object[]>

Export function createInMemoryStateAdapter() that returns an object implementing the StateAdapter interface above. Internally uses three Map<string, object> instances (one each for taskDefinitions, taskInstances, users), keyed by @id.

Conflict resolution per §5.1 (operator decision I7: apply LWW for BOTH saveTaskDefinition and saveTaskInstance; ignore §3.2 'never mutated' clause; ftm:version is informational only):
  Internal helper resolveConflict(existing, incoming):
    1. If !existing: return incoming
    2. Compare ftm:clientSequence. Higher wins.
    3. If equal, compare ftm:updatedAt (the @value string; ISO-8601 strings compare correctly lexicographically). Later wins.
    4. If both equal: incoming wins (idempotent re-save).
  
  Apply resolveConflict in saveTaskDefinition, saveTaskInstance, and saveUser. Add JSDoc note on saveUser explaining LWW also applies for consistency (SPEC §5.1 silent on User but interface symmetry).

listTaskDefinitions(filter): if filter.status present, return only entities where ftm:status === filter.status; else return all values.
listTaskInstances(filter): apply InstanceFilter — assignedTo, status (compare instance['ftm:completionState']['ftm:status']), taskDefinitionId (compare instance['ftm:taskDefinition']), fromDate / toDate (compare instance['ftm:dueAt']['@value']). Filters AND together.
listUsers(): return all values.

All methods return Promises (use async functions). State is process-local; not persisted across restarts (in-memory contract).

Read SPEC §6 and §6.1 (lines 343-396 of project/family-task-manager-spec.md) for OrchestrationAdapter requirements and the tier table. Read project/src/adapters/state/inMemoryStateAdapter.js for the established adapter-export pattern (createX factory returning interface). Report file paths and line ranges.

Create TWO new files. JavaScript ESM. No new dependencies. before: null for both.

File 1 - project/src/adapters/orchestration/tier0OrchestrationAdapter.js:

JSDoc typedef at top for OrchestrationAdapter interface:
  @typedef {Object} OrchestrationAdapter
    scheduleAt(isoTimestamp, callback) -> string handle
    scheduleInterval(intervalMs, callback) -> string handle
    cancel(handle): void
    onResume(currentTime): void

Export function createTier0OrchestrationAdapter() returning the interface. Implementation:
  Internal Map<string, {type: 'timeout'|'interval', nodeHandle: any}> keyed by string handle (use crypto.randomUUID()).
  scheduleAt(iso, cb): compute delayMs = new Date(iso).getTime() - Date.now(); if delayMs <= 0 invoke cb on nextTick / queueMicrotask immediately; else setTimeout(cb, delayMs). Store the Node timeout handle. Return UUID handle.
  scheduleInterval(ms, cb): setInterval(cb, ms). Store handle. Return UUID.
  cancel(handle): look up entry; if type 'timeout' clearTimeout(nodeHandle); if 'interval' clearInterval(nodeHandle); delete map entry.
  onResume(now): register the now timestamp on the adapter (no resume handlers in Tier 0 itself — the orchestration layer calls onResume; this is a no-op placeholder for future hooks). Document with JSDoc note that resume reconciliation is composed externally (SPEC §6.1).

JSDoc on the adapter should state: 'Background throttling is a known limitation per SPEC §6.1 Tier 0 — JavaScript timers are unreliable when a browser tab or PWA is backgrounded.'

File 2 - project/src/adapters/orchestration/testOrchestrationAdapter.js:

Export createTestOrchestrationAdapter() returning OrchestrationAdapter PLUS an extra tick(isoTimestamp) method.
Implementation:
  Internal arrays: timeouts = [{handle, fireAt: number ms, cb, fired: boolean}]; intervals = [{handle, intervalMs, lastFiredAt: number ms, cb, registered: number ms}].
  Internal logicalTime = 0 (set to new Date(...).getTime() on first tick or scheduleAt; start at scheduleAt's reference if needed). Track currentLogicalMs.
  scheduleAt(iso, cb): push timeout entry with fireAt = new Date(iso).getTime(); return handle.
  scheduleInterval(ms, cb): push interval entry; registered = currentLogicalMs (or 0); lastFiredAt = registered; return handle.
  cancel(handle): remove the entry from both arrays.
  onResume(now): update currentLogicalMs = new Date(now).getTime() (informational; tick is the real driver).
  tick(isoTimestamp): const targetMs = new Date(isoTimestamp).getTime();
    For timeouts: filter timeouts where fireAt <= targetMs AND !fired; sort ascending by fireAt; for each, set fired=true and invoke cb.
    For intervals: for each interval entry: compute how many intervals elapsed = Math.floor((targetMs - lastFiredAt) / intervalMs); fire that many times; update lastFiredAt += elapsed * intervalMs.
    Update currentLogicalMs = targetMs.
    NO real timers (setTimeout/setInterval) anywhere. Document this in JSDoc.
